pageText.html:
Our commitment to accessibility

The Guild, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel We want everyone who visits our website to be able to find information, explore the hotel and plan their stay with ease, whatever device or assistive technology they use.

We aim to follow recognised web accessibility guidance, such as the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), and to keep improving the site as it changes. This statement is a general placeholder and will be updated with fuller detail.

Feedback and contact: if you have difficulty using any part of this website, or need information in a different format, please get in touch through our contact page and we will do our best to help.

Measures We Take

Measures we aim to apply across the website include:

  • Clear headings and a logical page structure
  • Text alternatives for meaningful images
  • Keyboard access to links, menus and forms
  • Visible focus states on interactive elements
  • Readable text sizes and colour contrast
  • Layouts that adapt to different screen sizes
  • Descriptive link and button labels
  • Clearly labelled form fields
  • Compatibility with common screen readers and browsers
  • Ongoing reviews as new content is added

The Guild, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel

The Guild, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel This Privacy Notice describes our practices in connection with information that we collect through websites operated by us from which you are accessing this Privacy Notice (the “Websites”), through the software applications made available by us for use on or through computers and mobile devices (the “Apps”), and through our social media pages that we control from which you are accessing this Privacy Notice (collectively, our “Social Media Pages”), (collectively, including the Websites, the Apps and our Social Media Pages, the “Services”). This Privacy Notice also applies to our offline collection of information. The information you provide helps us to operate effectively and continually provide you with the best hospitality products, services and experiences.

Our privacy practices may vary among the countries in which we operate to reflect local practices and legal requirements. Please read the following to learn more about our privacy practices.

Your Acceptance of Our Privacy Notice: By using the Services, you accept the terms of this Privacy Notice and the ways we may use your information. If you do not accept the terms of this Notice, please do not continue to use the Services.

What Information Is Collected and How Is It Collected?

We may collect personal information (which is information that identifies you or relates to you as an identifiable person) about you such as your:

  • Name
  • Postal address (including billing and shipping addresses)
  • Telephone number
  • Email address
  • Credit and debit card number
  • Financial information
  • Profile picture
  • Social media account ID
  • Stay information
  • Communication preferences

As a YMCA, it became a destination of welcome and belonging for a growing military community, offering lodging, recreation, education and fellowship. Today, we’re proud stewards of that generous spirit of service, camaraderie and hospitality.

In 1924, following San Diego’s 1915 Panama-California Exhibition, George Marston commissioned architects Lincoln Rogers and Frank Stevenson to design a building that would become a turning point in the city’s architectural history.

pageText.html: Home to the Services

A postcard from the YMCA dated April 1945 bears the tagline “The Home Away From Home”. In nearly five decades as a YMCA, some eight million Army and Navy servicemen and women called it home, playground, living room, bowling alley, restaurant, boxing ring, checkers table, and much, much more. If you listen carefully, the walls of The Guild will tell a half-century of stories of joyous community, intimacy and connection.

pageText.html: THE GUILD OPENS ITS DOORS

After the YMCA closed its doors, the downtown landmark slumbered until it was reborn as The Guild, part of Marriott’s Tribute Portfolio. As a luxury hotel, it provided an oasis for the ever-growing number of visitors to “America’s Finest City.”
